title: ARWP Earned Discovery Practices
purpose: Turn a genuinely useful public asset into an audience-discovery plan without treating backlink acquisition, outreach volume or paid placement as ranking proof.

rules.claim: Promotion should start from content or a resource that is useful, original or materially differentiated for the intended audience rather than from a need to manufacture links.
rules.decision: Require an explicit original contribution and visible supporting evidence before recommending earned distribution as ready work. Unknown quality stays watch; a declared non-original/no-value asset fails closed.

rules.claim: Google's SEO Starter Guide explicitly lists social promotion, community engagement, advertising and word of mouth as ways to help interested people discover new content while warning that promotion can be overdone.
rules.decision: Recommend only declared channels with a real audience fit. Unknown fit stays watch; a channel declared irrelevant to the audience is excluded rather than used for volume.

rules.claim: Buying or selling links for ranking purposes, excessive reciprocal links, automated link creation, low-quality directory links and optimized forum-comment links are examples of link spam.
rules.decision: Block tactics whose stated goal is ranking manipulation, automated link creation, bulk forum/link posting or required reciprocal linking. Do not optimize for backlink count.

rules.claim: Advertising and sponsorship links are not inherently prohibited, but Google says paid links should be qualified so they do not pass ranking credit, including rel=sponsored or rel=nofollow.
rules.decision: Any paid/sponsored channel that can create a link must declare sponsored or nofollow qualification. Treat the placement as paid distribution, never earned authority.

rules.claim: Google warns that over-promotion can fatigue people and that automated/manipulative link creation violates spam policy; scaled low-value content used to manipulate linking or ranking signals is also prohibited.
rules.decision: Fail closed on mass automated posting/link creation and keep distribution tied to one canonical useful asset instead of manufacturing thin variants for channels or keywords.

rules.claim: Promotion is useful when it helps interested people discover the asset; raw outreach attempts or backlink counts are not evidence that Search rankings improved.
rules.decision: Require at least one audience/outcome measurement such as qualified referrals, subscribers, legitimate citations/references, direct/brand demand or owner-observed Search/AI visibility. Preserve before/after uncertainty and do not infer causality from one observation.
